summary_rationale: Ajmera Realty & Infra India Limited (ARIIL) exhibits strong operational momentum driven by the ongoing Mumbai residential upcycle, a successful pivot toward asset-light society redevelopment (JDA/DM), and disciplined balance-sheet deleveraging that has lowered consolidated debt-to-equity from historical peaks above 1.5x to 0.44x by September 2026. Pre-sales expanded 57% year-on-year to ₹1,701 crore in FY26, collections rose 71% to ₹1,103 crore, and weighted average borrowing costs fell below 11% to 10.75%. However, the company is fundamentally an urban property developer governed by multi-year real estate cycles, municipal approval lead times, and lumpy cash conversion. Over the ten-year period from FY17 through FY26, cumulative operating cash flow totaled ₹149 crore against cumulative net profit of ₹867 crore, reflecting continuous working-capital absorption into project execution and regulatory premiums. Value realization remains heavily hinged on the staged monetization of its crown-jewel Wadala land bank (~₹16,000 crore gross development value) and unsticking long-dated conversion hurdles at Kanjurmarg.
